author: Swinhoe, 1863

art.subject: Japanese Leaf Warbler (Phylloscopus xanthodryas), adult, as seen on Korean islands during spring migration: crown and upperparts fairly bright yellowish-green; long yellowish-white supercilium that stops short of the forehead; dark olive eye-stripe running to the bill base; ear-coverts mottled olive and yellow; wings darker with green edges and a narrow yellowish-white bar on the greater coverts, sometimes a second faint bar on the median coverts; underparts whitish strongly washed yellow, most yellow on the throat, flanks and undertail coverts. Bill dark with a pale orange-yellow base to the lower mandible; dark eye; legs pale brownish.
art.pose: foraging among fresh leaves in the canopy, side view
art.scene: deciduous trees on a Korean offshore island during spring migration in late May; no people, buildings or text
art.build: Medium-sized leaf warbler, smaller than a sparrow but larger and longer-winged than Yellow-browed Warbler, with a rather flat crown and a fairly stout, pointed bill shorter than the head. Legs medium length, pale. Long wings with a long primary projection; the wingtips reach well down the tail. Tail medium length, square-ended. Forages actively in the canopy, picking insects from leaves.
avoid: Do not paint it dull grey-green with whitish underparts like Arctic Warbler (Phylloscopus borealis); this species is yellower above and below.
Do not paint a pale crown stripe (Eastern Crowned Warbler).
Do not paint two bold white wing-bars (Two-barred Warbler); the bar is narrow and the second is faint or absent.
